revisions.title: From Praise to Inquiry
revisions.body: I hear this opening as a rehearsal of philosophical method rather than a verdict on Theaetetus. On that reading, praise arrives first, but Socrates treats neither resemblance nor reputation as self-validating: the speaker’s competence must be tested, and the student must be willing to display himself. The scene’s pressure lies in turning admiration into examination—an invitation, not yet a conclusion.

revisions.title: A doctrine turned against itself
revisions.body: One way to hear this passage is as a pressure test of Protagoras’ measure: if every appearance is true for the person who has it, then the appearance that the doctrine is wrong must also count. The measure has become answerable to judgments it cannot simply dismiss.

revisions.title: The wax tablet: a provisional model of error
revisions.body: One way to read the wax tablet is as a trial model for error. It invites us to picture a mistake as a wrong fit between an imprint and a present perception. But that is an opening proposal, not a settled result: the dialogue must still test whether this image can bear the weight placed on it.

revisions.title: When the distinction collapses
revisions.body: One way I hear this stretch is as a stress test for the dream’s attractive division between unknowable elements and knowable combinations. Socrates makes the listener choose between two pictures of the syllable, then shows why neither preserves that division. The pressure falls not on defining the syllable once and for all, but on asking whether the theory can keep its promised gap intact.

body: "I read Socrates as closing both routes by which the dream tries to separate knowledge from its elements. If a syllable is a whole made of letters, knowing the whole requires the letters, so both become knowable and expressible. If instead the syllable is a single indivisible form, it has the same status as an element: neither can be explained or known. On either reading, the promised gap between unknowable letters and knowable syllables disappears."
